key_insight: PEA organic spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects, slowing degradation of 2D lead iodide perovskites under ambient light and thermal stress compared with BA spacers.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA₂PbI₄ and PEA₂PbI₄ perovskites under ambient light and thermal stress.
Used confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to investigate degradation.
Examined morphology, lattice defects, and freshly exfoliated nanoflake luminescence.
evidence_signal: Both materials showed comparable initial room-temperature luminescence and degradation into PbI₂ and metallic Pb, but PEA₂PbI₄ degraded more slowly.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative stability gains or solar-cell performance tests, so improved material stability does not establish longer device lifetimes.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
